《上海泰晤士报》，1936年1月7日，星期二

警员将以谋杀罪名受审

被告称将男子放入河中“乞丐船”；保释申请待向大英按察使司衙门提出期间撤销保释

据昨日早上主持审讯并听取控方陈述的大英按察使 C. H. Haines 先生所作决定，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）警长 E. W. Peters 和试用警长 W. A. Judd 将因谋杀乞丐毛德标（Mau Tuh-piau）一案在大英按察使司衙门受审。据称，二人于12月1日凌晨将该乞丐抛入虹口港。

在决定将二人以谋杀罪交付审判时，Haines 先生表示，鉴于他的决定，保释事宜已不在其职权范围内，二人将在候审期间被羁押。辩方律师 Reeks 先生表示，他将向上级法院申请保释。

针对两人的相同指控内容为：“兹指控你等于1935年12月1日在上海谋杀毛德标（Mau Tuh-piau）。”

两人对指控回应称：“不认罪。”

辩方律师 H. A. Reeks 先生表示，他们的案件将留待上级法院审理，但称二人希望各自作简短陈述。因此，法庭向他们发出警告并记录了他们的陈述。随后，二人站在被告席上，就此事向法庭作了首次陈述。

将乞丐放上船

Peters 警长称，12月1日凌晨2点44分过后不久，他陪同 Judd 警长去接一名躺在百老汇路（Point Road）与新嘉坡路（Singkeipang Road）拐角处的生病乞丐。他们将其扶上车，前往圣路加医院，但在途中，该乞丐似乎苏醒过来。由于圣路加医院除非病情非常严重，否则不接收乞丐病例，他便命令车辆沿斐伦路（Fearon Road）折返，以便将该乞丐安置在停泊于虹口港的一艘“乞丐船”上。他说，他们并未将乞丐扔进河里，而是将他放在其中一艘船上，当他们离开时，他仍在船上。

Peters 警长解释了他决定陪同 Judd 警长前往的原因，即 Judd 最近才调至嘉兴路地区，不熟悉街道情况。

Judd 警长的陈述与 Peters 的相似。

死于医院

在 Reeks 先生就证据的可采性进行法律辩论后——Haines 先生称他会将这些要点记录在案——警察法庭的审讯休庭。

控方案情的简要概述如下：凌晨2点45分左右，一名华捕注意到百老汇路与新嘉坡路拐角处有一名生病的乞丐，遂电话通知嘉兴路巡捕房。Peters 警长离开岗位，与 Judd 乘车前往该地。他们带上乞丐，将其放在汽车踏板上，绕行后进入斐伦路，停车并将该男子抛入虹口港。一名小贩和其他几人救起了该男子，虹口巡捕房的一名警员叫来救护车，将乞丐送往圣路加医院，数日后他因双侧肺炎去世。

档案
JAS
'37年1月

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE USE OF YEN NOTES IN SHANGHAI.

With reference to the circulation of Yen notes
by the Japanese residents in Shanghai as from January 1, the
First Special District Citizens Federation the other day
notified all its branches not to accept these notes.
Acting on a report from the Hongkew branch that
Japanese residents are tendering Yen notes to Chinese shops
for use, the Federation has decided to call an urgent meeting
on the afternoon of January 10 to discuss concrete measures
to deal with the matter.

Siao Chen Pao (小晨报), a mosquito newspaper, publishes
the following brief comment:-

THE CASE AGAINST TWO FOREIGN POLICE OFFICERS

In December last year, Foreign Sergeant
Peters and Probationary Sergeant Judd of the Shanghai
Municipal Police threw a Chinese beggar into the Soochow
Creek. The two men appeared on remand in the Police
Court at 9 a.m. yesterday when they were committed for
trial on a charge of manslaughter before the British
Supreme Court. A Chinese Judge will be present to watch
the proceedings.
The existence of the unequal treaties has
resulted in numerous disputes between Chinese and
foreigners. Furthermore, the existence of the Settlements
administration constitutes an infringement of our national
rights. After the revolution in the 15th Year of the
Chinese Republic, conditions have gradually improved
as a result of the establishment of the Special District
Court. There occurred unexpectedly an incident in which
foreign Police officers had recklessly and
unreasonably treated human beings. Is not such a state
of affairs intolerable?
It is of course too early to discuss the
question of the extradition of the two officers, but
we however hope that the entire Chinese community will
urge the British Consulate as well as the Chinese Judge
who will watch the proceedings to uphold justice. It
is only in this way that the illegal practices on the
part of the foreign sergeants can be prevented.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

SELECTION OF STUDENTS' DELEGATES TO NANKING

The local universities and middle schools
had previously been instructed by the authorities to
commence the winter vacation earlier. All local universities
and middle schools resumed classes yesterday and are now
making preparations for examinations.
The order of the Central Authorities to
select representatives to proceed to Nanking will be
observed by local universities and middle schools.

两名外籍警官之案件

去年12月，上海公共租界工部局警务处外籍警长 Peters 和试用警长 Judd 将一名中国乞丐抛入苏州河。二人于昨日上午9时在警察法庭受审，被交付英国最高法院以过失杀人罪受审。一名中国法官将出席旁听诉讼程序。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 31, 1935

Doctor Testifies Fresh
Pneumonia Signs Seen
In Lungs Of Beggar

Sent Specimens To
Public Health
Department

DECISION EXPECTED
IN CASE MONDAY

Supreme Court Clerk
Tells Of Talking
To Deceased

That signs of fresh pneumonia which have contributed to death, and which could have been caused by immersion in the waters such as those of Hongkew Creek, were found in the lungs of Mau Teh-piau, beggar, was the gist of testimony offered by Dr. S. K. Squires, physician, before Registrar C. H. Haines in H. M. British Police Court yesterday morning. Dr. Squires testified as witness for the prosecution in the action brought against Sergeant E. W. Peters and Probationary Sergeant W. A. Judd, charged with committing assault against a beggar by throwing him into Hongkew Creek.

Mr. John McNeill concluded the case of the prosecution yesterday, but no formal charges were framed by Registrar Haines against the two sergeants. The Registrar stated that he wished time to read over the evidence and continued the case until Monday, January 6.

Dr. Squires testified that on December 6 he had attended a post mortem held on the remains of Mau Teh-piau, who died the day previous at St. Luke's Hospital where he had been brought for treatment after what had apparently been sudden immersion in water. The doctor stated that he did not take part in the post mortem but stood and watched the Chinese doctor who actually conducted the work.

He continued that he took specimens from the dead man's lungs, placed them in small jars and sent them to the Public Health Department laboratories for preparation for examination by microscope. The doctor then produced the laboratory report and the three specimens, contained in small boxes, placing them in the custody of the court as exhibits.

Fresh Pneumonia Present

Questioned by Mr. John McNeill, in charge of the prosecution, as to whether he had formed an opinion of what the beggar's condition might have been a few days prior to death, the doctor stated that he had. He stated that sudden immersion in water would be harmful to a man in the beggar's condition, adding, upon being further questioned, that such immersion might aggravate illness already existing or cause the development of fresh pneumonia in other parts of the lungs. He stated that the examination had revealed that fresh pneumonia was present. He also stated that death was caused by pneumonia.

The morning session was featured by conflicting testimony of two witnesses who had interviewed the beggar shortly before his death. S.P.C. 340, Zuh Kwei-tsung, declared that he had gone to St. Luke's and had questioned the beggar as to how it happened that he was in Hongkew Creek. The constable asked the man if "he was poor, had nothing to eat, and jumped into the creek," it was brought out. The constable stated that the man answered "yes."

It was brought out during the cross-examination of this witness that the beggar came from Nanking while his interrogator comes from Peiping.

Opposed to this testimony was the evidence submitted by Mr. Anthony Ricketts, chief clerk of H.B.M. Supreme Court. This witness stated that he questioned Mau Teh-piau on order from the court and through an interpreter. He stated that the beggar was made aware of his danger and that there was no hope for his recovery before he was questioned.

"I Am Going To Die"

"I think I am going to die," was the beggar's reply to the first question put to him by the clerk, it was stated.

The clerk continued that he asked the beggar whether or not he had been thrown into the creek. He quoted the sick man.

"Yes, I was thrown into the creek by two foreigners," the patient stated in reply. The man continued, the clerk said, that he could not remember what time he saw them nor could he recognize them. It then developed that the two accused had been brought before the man for identification but he could not identify them. Asked if he had seen a car with two foreigners, the beggar was said to have answered "Yes."

Chinese Detective Sub-Inspector Yao Yuen-loong, who acted as interpreter for Mr. Ricketts, was called to the witness box in the afternoon and testified under cross examination that the beggar could speak very well and did not talk in monosyllables.

Other witnesses who testified during the morning session were Dr. James H. Blakelock, of the Public Health Department, and Ting Sai-tung, interne at St. Luke's Hospital. The latter stated that he had attended the patient. Dr. Blakelock submitted as evidence his report to Dr. S. K. Squires regarding the laboratory examination of the lung specimens from Mau Teh-piau.

《字林西报》，1935年12月31日，星期二

医生提供新证词
乞丐肺部发现
新发肺炎迹象

样本已送交
公共卫生处

预计周一
对此案作出裁决

最高法院书记官
讲述与死者
谈话经过

S. K. Squires 医生昨天上午在英国警察法庭向验尸官 C. H. Haines 提供的证词要点是：在乞丐毛德标（Mau Teh-piau）的肺部发现了导致其死亡的新发肺炎迹象，而这种肺炎可能是由浸入虹口港（Hongkew Creek）这类水域引起的。Squires 医生作为控方证人出庭，此案是针对警长 E. W. Peters 和见习警长 W. A. Judd 提起的诉讼，指控他们将一名乞丐扔进虹口港，犯有袭击罪。

John McNeill 先生昨天结束了控方的举证，但验尸官 Haines 尚未对两名警长提出正式指控。验尸官表示，他希望有时间审阅证据，并将案件延期至1月6日星期一审理。

Squires 医生作证说，他在12月6日参加了对毛德标遗体的尸检，毛德标于前一天在圣路加医院（St. Luke's Hospital）去世，此前他因显然突然浸入水中而被送往该医院接受治疗。医生说，他并未参与尸检，而是站在一旁观看实际进行操作的中国医生。

他接着说，他从死者肺部提取了样本，放入小瓶中，并送往公共卫生处实验室，以便制备后通过显微镜进行检查。随后，医生出示了实验室报告以及装在小盒子里的三份样本，并将它们作为物证交由法庭保管。

存在新发肺炎

负责控诉的 John McNeill 先生询问他，对于乞丐在死前几天的状况是否已形成看法，医生回答说已形成看法。他表示，对于像该乞丐那样身体状况的人，突然浸入水中是有害的，并在进一步受询时补充说，这种浸入可能会加剧既有的疾病，或导致肺部其他部位发展新发肺炎。他说，检查结果显示存在新发肺炎。他还表示，死因是肺炎。

上午庭审的特点是两名在乞丐死前不久曾与其交谈的证人提供了相互矛盾的证词。上海公共租界巡捕房警员编号340朱桂宗（Zuh Kwei-tsung，音译）宣称，他曾前往圣路加医院，并询问乞丐是如何落入虹口港的。据披露，这名巡捕问此人是否“因为贫穷，没东西吃，所以跳进河里”。巡捕称，那人回答“是”。

在对这名证人进行交叉盘问时披露，该乞丐来自南京，而讯问者来自北平。

与此证词相反的是英国驻华最高法院首席书记官 Anthony Ricketts 先生提交的证据。这位证人表示，他是奉法庭之命并通过一名翻译讯问毛德标的。他说，在讯问之前，已让乞丐知晓其危险处境，且康复无望。

“我要死了”

据称，书记官向乞丐提出的第一个问题得到的回答是：“我想我要死了。”

书记官接着说，他问乞丐是否曾被扔进河里。他引用了那位病人的话。

病人回答说：“是的，我被两个外国人扔进了河里。”书记官说，那人接着表示，他不记得见到他们的时间，也无法认出他们。随后的情况表明，两名被告曾被带到此人面前供其辨认，但他无法指认他们。当被问及是否见过一辆载有两名外国人的汽车时，据说乞丐回答“见过”。

下午传召了担任 Ricketts 先生翻译的华探副督察姚元龙（Yao Yuen-loong，音译）出庭作证，他在交叉盘问下作证说，该乞丐很会说话，并非只讲单音节词。

上午出庭作证的其他证人包括公共卫生处的 James H. Blakelock 医生和圣路加医院的实习生丁赛东（Ting Sai-tung，音译）。后者表示他曾诊治过该病人。Blakelock 医生提交了他给 S. K. Squires 医生的报告作为证据，该报告涉及对毛德标肺部样本的实验室检查结果。

（档案
JHS
1935年12月81号）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 28, 1935

INSPECTOR TESTIFIES
IN BEGGAR CASE

Man In Charge Room Not
Allowed To Leave
Duty, He Says

Another full day in H. M. Police Court was taken yesterday in testimony and cross-examination of witnesses for the prosecution in the case against Sergeant E. W. Peters and Probationary Sergeant W. A. Judd, who are being examined on charges of assault and unlawful killing of a beggar, Mau Tuh-piau.

The policemen are alleged to have thrown the beggar into Hongkew Creek on the early morning of December 1. Their alleged victim died at St. Luke's Hospital three days later from double pneumonia, according to a verdict returned at an inquest by the Chinese authorities.

Inspector G. J. Bennett, recalled again as a witness, said that he commenced investigation of the case when a detective came to him with certain information on the day following the alleged assault. He said he questioned the driver of the car used by the policemen to pick up the beggar and afterwards called Captain Kennedy, S.M.P. official, to discuss the case. Witness avowed that he had examined the record books of Kashing Road Station, of which he is in charge. He said that Sergeant Peters was on charge room duty on the night in question. Questioned, he said unequivocally that the man on charge room duty was not supposed to leave the station. Inspector Bennett told also of arranging to dredge that section of Hongkew Creek between the Yalu and Yuhang Road bridges.

Doctors Testify

Dr. A. W. Tucker, in charge at St. Luke's Hospital, said that a man answering the description of the beggar was brought to the Hospital on December 1. His name was entered as Mau Tuhpiau.

Dr. Hwang Ming-sing, resident physician, said that he had signed the death certificate, while Lun Ding-wong, an interne, said that he had seen the man upon admittance to the Hospital. His clothes were wet and dirty and his body was very cold.

Zung Tsoh-ling, a nurse, said that he had ordered student nurses to give the man a bath on the day of admittance and, on the following day, had prescribed a shave.

Mr. John McNeill, prosecuting, said that he hoped to complete his case by another full day's hearing which will be taken up on Monday morning.

《上海泰晤士报》，1935年12月28日，星期六

督察在乞丐案中
作证

他说值班室负责人
不得离开
岗位

昨天，英国警察法庭又用了一整天时间，听取并交叉盘问了控方证人，这些证人是在针对警长 E. W. Peters 和见习警长 W. A. Judd 的案件中作证的，二人因涉嫌袭击及非法杀害一名名叫毛德标（Mau Tuh-piau）的乞丐而受审。

据称，这两名警察在12月1日凌晨将这名乞丐扔进了虹口港。据中国当局验尸后作出的裁决，他们的所谓受害者在三天后死于圣路加医院，死因为双肺肺炎。

G. J. Bennett 督察再次作为证人被传召，他说，在所谓袭击发生的第二天，当一名侦探向他提供某些信息时，他便开始调查此案。他说他讯问了警察用来接走乞丐的那辆汽车的司机，随后致电工部局警务处官员 Kennedy 上尉讨论此案。证人声称，他查阅了他所负责的嘉善路捕房的记录簿。他说，Peters 警长在事发当晚负责值班室工作。在被问及此事时，他明确地说，负责值班室工作的人员不应离开捕房。Bennett 督察还讲述了安排疏浚鸭绿江路与余杭路桥之间那段虹口港河道的事宜。

医生作证

圣路加医院主管医生 A. W. Tucker 医生说，12月1日，一名符合乞丐描述的男子被送到医院。他的名字登记为毛德标（Mau Tuhpiau）。

驻院医生黄明兴（Hwang Ming-sing，音译）医生说，他签署了死亡证明，而实习生伦定旺（Lun Ding-wong，音译）说，他在该男子入院时见过他。他的衣服又湿又脏，身体非常冰冷。

护士钟佐灵（Zung Tsoh-ling，音译）说，他在入院当天命令实习护士给该男子洗澡，并在第二天吩咐为其刮胡子。

控方律师 John McNeill 先生说，他希望在周一上午进行的另一次全天听证会上完成控方举证。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 28, 1935

Inspector Started Probe Of
Beggar Case Immediately

Bennett Testifies In British Court That He
Questioned Driver Of Car, Then
Examined Station Record Books

That he took up the investigation of the case upon receiving a report from a Chinese detective-inspector stationed at the Kashing Road Police Station, comprised what was perhaps the most important piece of evidence submitted by Inspector G. J. Bennett testifying at the continued hearing of charges of assault against Sergeant E. W. Peters and Probationary Sergeant W. A. Judd before Registrar C. H. Haines in H. M. Police Court yesterday morning.

The two accused are alleged to have thrown a beggar named Mau Teh-piau into Hongkew Creek early in the morning of December 1. He is believed to be the same man who died at St. Luke's Hospital three days later and over whom inquest was held at the Fearon Road Mortuary and a verdict of death by double pneumonia was returned.

Inspector Bennett was in the witness box all morning, except for about 30 minutes taken up by Mr. H. A. Reeks, counsel for the defense, in an argument on technicalities. The inspector stated that he commenced investigation of the case when a detective inspector came to him with certain information. This was on the day after the alleged assault had taken place. He continued that he called the driver of the car the two sergeants had used to go and pick up the beggar.

Peters On Duty

At previous hearings of the case, the chauffeur testified that he had seen the two accused throw the beggar into the creek. Inspector Bennett continued that he questioned the chauffeur and afterwards called Captain Kennedy, of the S.M.P., and asked the latter to come to the Kashing Road Station.

Inspector Bennett declared that he examined the record books of the station in conducting his investigation, adding that Sergeant Peters was on charge room duty that night and was not supposed to leave the station. He also declared that he had arranged to have that section of Hongkew Creek between Yalu and Yuhang Road bridges dragged with the assistance of the River Police.

The afternoon was largely taken up with the cross-examination of doctors and nurses from St. Luke's Hospital. Dr. Augustine Washington Tucker, senior doctor in charge, testified that a man answering the description of the beggar was brought to the hospital about 3.30 a.m. December 1. The man's name was given to the hospital as Mau Teh-piau.

Death Certificate Signed

Dr. Hwang Ming-sing, resident physician at the hospital, testified that he had signed the death certificate while Lun Ding-wong, interne, told the court that he had seen the man upon his admittance to the hospital, had noticed that his clothes were wet and dirty and that his body, legs and arms were "cold as ice." He thought that the man might have been drowning before being brought to the hospital.

Zung Tsoh-ling, male nurse at the hospital, testified that he had ordered student nurses to give the man a bath on the day of admittance and that on the following day had ordered that he be given a shave.

Hearing of the case will be continued at 10 a.m. Monday morning. Mr. John McNeill, in charge of the prosecution, informed the court that he hoped that he would be able to complete his case before Monday evening.

《字林西报》，1935年12月28日，星期六

督察立即启动
乞丐案调查

Bennett 在英国法庭作证称，他讯问了汽车司机，随后
查阅了捕房记录簿

G. J. Bennett 督察昨天上午在英国警察法庭就针对警长 E. W. Peters 和见习警长 W. A. Judd 的袭击指控继续进行的听证会上作证，他所提交的或许是最重要的一项证据是：他在收到驻扎在嘉善路捕房的一名华探副督察的报告后，随即展开了对该案的调查。

据称，这两名被告在12月1日凌晨将一名名叫毛德标（Mau Teh-piau）的乞丐扔进了虹口港。人们相信他就是三天后在圣路加医院去世、并在斐伦路（Fearon Road）停尸房接受验尸、死因被裁定为双肺肺炎的同一个人。

除了辩护律师 H. A. Reeks 先生就技术性问题进行辩论占用的约30分钟外，Bennett 督察整个上午都在证人席上。督察表示，当一名侦探副督察向他提供某些信息时，他便开始调查此案。这发生在所谓袭击事件的第二天。他接着说，他讯问了两名警长用来去接乞丐的那辆汽车的司机。

Peters 在值班

在此前对该案的听证中，司机作证说，他看到两名被告将乞丐扔进河里。Bennett 督察继续说，他讯问了司机，随后致电工部局警务处的 Kennedy 上尉，请后者到嘉善路捕房来。

Bennett 督察宣称，他在调查过程中查阅了捕房的记录簿，并补充说，Peters 警长当晚在值班室值班，按规定不应离开捕房。他还宣称，他已在河浜巡逻队的协助下，安排拖网打捞鸭绿江路与余杭路桥之间那段虹口港河道。

下午的时间主要用于交叉盘问来自圣路加医院的医生和护士。资深主管医生 Augustine Washington Tucker 医生作证说，12月1日凌晨约3点30分，一名符合乞丐描述的男子被送到医院。该男子向医院报出的名字是毛德标（Mau Teh-piau）。

签署死亡证明

医院驻院医生黄明兴（Hwang Ming-sing，音译）医生作证说，他签署了死亡证明，而实习生伦定旺（Lun Ding-wong，音译）告诉法庭，他在该男子入院时见过他，注意到他的衣服又湿又脏，而且他的身体、腿和手臂“冷如冰”。他认为该男子在被送到医院之前可能已经溺水。

医院男护士钟佐灵（Zung Tsoh-ling，音译）作证说，他在入院当天命令实习护士给该男子洗澡，并在第二天吩咐为其刮胡子。

案件听证将于周一上午10点继续。控方负责人 John McNeill 先生告知法庭，他希望能在周一晚上之前完成控方举证。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 21, 1935

Accused Made Statements
In Case Of Sick Beggar

High Police Officials Tell Of Investigations
Following Report On Judd And Peters;
Entry In Charge Book Admitted

The testimony of Assistant Commissioner E. R. Kennedy and Inspector G. J. Bennett, of Kashing Road Police Station, featured yesterday's hearing of the preliminary examination in H.M. Police Court of Probationary Sergeant W. A. Judd and Sergeant F. W. Peters, who are charged with the unlawful killing of a Chinese beggar by throwing him into Hongkew Creek.

Mr. Kennedy and Mr. Bennett were both present when Peters and Judd were brought up departmentally concerning a report about them. Judd was cautioned and told that he need not make a statement but that if he did make a statement, it would be taken down in writing and might be used against him.

Judd said there was nothing in the matter, but that he would like time to think it over.

Peters made a brief statement verbally, which was taken down in writing. In response to a question concerning an entry in the Kashing Road Station charge book—"upon arrival the beggar had left"—Peters admitted that the handwriting was his own.

All of this took place on the afternoon of December 2, and at 8 o'clock that night Peters and Judd came to Inspector Bennett's office and submitted two statements. At this time they were again cautioned that they need make no statement.

Removal Of Beggar

Corroborative testimony concerning the removal of the beggar from the creek bank to St. Luke's Hospital was heard from several witnesses. Yang Wha-zung, C.D.C. 993 said he was walking his beat on Fearon Road near Haining Road when he heard the call—"save life." He ran and found a Chinese lying on the bank of the creek. He telephoned to Hongkew Station. He was told a car had knocked the man down into the creek. He took down the car number given him by a hawker, but the hawker wrote his own name in the book.

Han Dong-foh, C.P.C. 1665, told of getting a report from C.P.C. 993 on the night in question and reporting to the officer on duty. Chu Ming-kung, interpreter at Hongkew Station, identified entries he had made in the street telephone book concerning the report. Inspector J. J. Hourihan, in charge of ambulances at Hongkew Brigade, told of finding a Chinese on the bank of Hongkew Creek in Fearon Road. The man was very wet, shivering and groaning. They stripped his clothes off, wrapped him in blankets and took him to St. Luke's Hospital.

Dragging Creek

Probationary Sergeant John Deaville said that on the morning on December 3 he went out with a Chinese detective constable of the River Police to watch dragging operations in Hongkew Creek near the East Yuhang Road Bridge. After a little while, he noticed the detective talking to a Chinese woman and a Chinese man. Then the detective reported to him, as a result of which he telephoned to Inspector Bennett.

Tsang Zung-see said she had seen two men lifting another man out of the water. Later, she said, police came to make inquiries.

Adjournment was made until Friday, December 27. Mr. John McNeill, prosecuting, said he hoped to finish his case on that day.

《字林西报》，1935年12月21日，星期六

被告作出陈述
关于患病乞丐一案

高级警务官员讲述在有关朱德（Judd）和彼得斯（Peters）的报告之后的调查情况；
承认在值班日志中的记录

昨天，在英国驻华法院进行的对见习警佐 W. A. 朱德（W. A. Judd）和警佐 F. W. 彼得斯（F. W. Peters）的预审听证会上，助理总监 E. R. 肯尼迪（E. R. Kennedy）和嘉兴路巡捕房督察 G. J. 贝内特（G. J. Bennett）的证词成为焦点。二人被控将一名中国乞丐扔进虹口港，致其非法死亡。

肯尼迪先生和贝内特先生均在彼得斯和朱德因有关他们的报告而被部门传唤时在场。朱德受到告诫，被告知他无需作出陈述，但如果他作出陈述，将被书面记录下来，并可能用作对他不利的证据。

朱德称此事并无实质内容，但他希望有时间考虑一下。

彼得斯作了简短的口头陈述，并被书面记录下来。当被问及嘉兴路巡捕房值班日志中的一条记录——“到达时乞丐已离开”——时，彼得斯承认该笔迹是他自己的。

这一切发生在12月2日下午，当晚8点，彼得斯和朱德来到贝内特督察的办公室，提交了两份陈述书。此时他们再次受到告诫，称他们无需作出陈述。

移走乞丐

几位证人提供了关于将乞丐从河岸移至圣路加医院（St. Luke's Hospital）的佐证证词。华捕993号杨华宗（Yang Wha-zung，音译）说，当他正在海宁路附近的斐伦路（Fearon Road）巡逻时，听到有人喊“救命”。他跑过去，发现一名中国人躺在河岸边。他打电话给虹口巡捕房。对方告诉他，一辆汽车将该男子撞入河中。他记下了小贩告诉他的车牌号，但该小贩在登记簿上写下了自己的名字。

华捕1665号韩东发（Han Dong-foh，音译）讲述了在事发当晚收到华捕993号的报告并向值班警官汇报的情况。虹口巡捕房的翻译朱明公（Chu Ming-kung，音译）指认了他在街道电话记录本中就该报告所作的记录。虹口分队负责救护车的 J. J. 霍里汉（J. J. Hourihan）督察讲述了在斐伦路的虹口港岸边发现一名中国人的经过。该男子浑身湿透，瑟瑟发抖，呻吟不止。他们脱掉他的衣服，用毯子将他包裹起来，送往圣路加医院。

打捞河道

见习警佐约翰·迪维尔（John Deaville）说，12月3日上午，他与一名水上警察局的华人侦探警员一起外出，观察在东余杭路桥附近的虹口港进行的打捞作业。过了一会儿，他注意到该侦探正在与一名中国妇女和一名中国男子交谈。随后，侦探向他报告，他因此打电话给贝内特督察。

曾宗氏（Tsang Zung-see，音译）说她曾看到两名男子将另一名男子从水中抬出。后来她说，警察前来询问。

休庭至12月27日（星期五）。公诉人约翰·麦克尼尔（John McNeill）先生表示，他希望在那天结束本案的审理。

December 17, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

China Times published the following comment on Dec. 15:-
TWO FOREIGN POLICEMEN THROW A BEGGAR INTO A CREEK.

On the first of this month a man named Ma Teh Piao (馬德標), native of Nanking, lay on Sinkeepang Road and Point Road, suffering from illness. He was discovered by a Chinese policeman, on patrol duty, who reported the matter to the Kashing Road Station. Two foreign Sergeants, Peters and Juid, proceeded to the said locality and placed the man in their car. Whilst passing by Fearon Road and Yalu Road, they suddenly ordered the driver, a Chinese policeman, to stop, after which they threw Ma Teh Piao into the creek. The act was witnessed by a vegetable hawker named Sung Ching Sung (孫金生), who, after borrowing a bamboo stick from a boat moored in the creek, succeeded in rescuing Ma Teh Piao out of the creek. Sung reported the matter to a Chinese policeman of Hongkew Police Station and Ma was removed to St. Luke's Hospital where, however, he died later.

Since this case of cruelty was made known, the Police brought an action against the two guilty foreign policemen in the British Consular Court. So far it is not known what the verdict will be. We are greatly astonished to witness such exceptional cruelty; firstly as it has been committed by "civilized" Britishers who sent a sick person to his death instead of rendering him immediate relief in human sympathy; secondly as even a passing-by hawker knows it to be his duty to give a helping hand, the two Britishers, being police officers, failed to fulfil this duty and remove this person to hospital for treatment but instead they hastened his death by cruel means.

On one hand, we naturally admit that the action of these two foreign policemen cannot be representatives of the spirit of the entire body of foreign policemen or Britishers, but on the other we are of the opinion that these culprits should be severely dealt with as a deterrent to others, and that the Police Department, which is responsible for the training of its members, cannot evade the responsibility for having entrusted the duty of a policeman to such cruel and inhuman persons, even though it has initiated the prosecution against the culprits. It is deemed to be of the greatest necessity that the Police should conduct a strict enquiry as to whether or not there still exist other cruel and inhuman members among its personnel, and that it should make an official declaration on this point in order to appease the minds of the public and to protect their safety.

（批：§5. Please let me know the name of the editor and address of this newspaper. Why do they persist in commenting on a case still under trial? JKS）

1935年12月17日。下午译文。

《时事新报》于12月15日发表了以下评论：
两名外籍警察将乞丐扔进河里。

本月一日，一名名叫马德标（Ma Teh Piao）的南京籍男子病卧在新闸路与北河南路（Point Road，音译，注：此处原文Point Road通常指北河南路或附近路段，依当时习惯译法），身体不适。他被一名正在巡逻的中国警察发现，该警察将此情况报告给嘉兴路巡捕房。两名外籍警佐，彼得斯（Peters）和朱伊德（Juid，即Judd），前往上述地点，将该男子带上他们的汽车。当经过斐伦路（Fearon Road）和鸭绿江路（Yalu Road，音译，注：可能指乍浦路或附近，依音译保留）时，他们突然命令司机（一名中国警察）停车，随后他们将马德标扔进河里。这一行为被一名名叫孙金生（Sung Ching Sung）的菜贩目睹，他从停泊在河里的一艘船上借了一根竹竿，成功将马德标从河中救出。孙某向虹口巡捕房的一名中国警察报告了此事，马某被送往圣路加医院，但后来在那里去世。

自从这起残忍案件曝光以来，警方在英国领事法庭对这两名有罪的外籍警察提起诉讼。目前尚不知判决结果如何。我们对此种异常的残忍行为感到极为震惊；首先，这种行为是由所谓的“文明”英国人犯下的，他们没有出于人道同情给予即时救助，反而将病人送向死亡；其次，即使是路过的小贩都知道伸出援手是自己的责任，而这两名身为警察的英国人却未能履行这一职责，将该人送往医院治疗，反而通过残忍的手段加速了他的死亡。

一方面，我们自然承认，这两名外籍警察的行为不能代表整个外籍警察队伍或英国人的精神，但另一方面，我们认为应严厉惩处这些罪犯，以儆效尤，而且负责培训其成员的警务处，即使已对罪犯提起公诉，也不能推卸将警察职责托付给如此残忍和不人道者的责任。人们认为，警方极有必要严格调查其人员中是否仍存在其他残忍和不人道的成员，并就此发表正式声明，以安抚公众情绪并保障他们的安全。

（批注：§5. 请告诉我该报编辑的姓名和地址。他们为何坚持评论仍在审理中的案件？JKS）

THE CHINA PRESS. FRIDAY, DECEMBER 20, 1935

Statements Questioned In
Dying Beggar Case

Written Statement Of Police Chauffeur Admitted
As Evidence; Distinction Of "Falling In
Water" Argued By Defence Counsel

Argument by counsel and cross-examination of witnesses who are alleged to have pulled Mau Tuh-piau, a sick beggar, out of Hongkew Creek in the early morning of November 30 occupied yesterday morning's hearing of the case against Sergeant E. W. Peters and Probationary Sergeant W. A. Judd, S.M.P. The men are arraigned before H. M. Magistrate (Mr. C. H. Haines) for preliminary examination on charges of assault and unlawful killing.

A written statement made by Doo Tsung-pu, C. P. C. 3067, on December 2 to Inspector Bennett, and which was the cause of considerable argument by Mr. H. A. Reeks, for the defence, who wanted it produced, was put in as evidence.

Recalled, witness said he thought the statement he made previously (the written one) was much the same as his story in court. He said he had not stated previously that he actually saw the beggar strike the water. He saw him thrown. He maintained his written statement did not say he actually saw the beggar strike the water.

He also said he heard but did not see the splash.

Helped Save Man

Kwok Sai-yuen, a shopkeeper of 491 Fearon Road, said he was getting ready for bed on the night in question when he heard someone outside calling "save life." He ran downstairs and saw his neighbour, Sung Ching-sun, pulling a man alongside the creek. He helped him to get the man ashore and then a Chinese policeman came and called an ambulance. Sung Ching-sun made a report to the policeman and then the ambulance came.

Cross - examination of Sung Ching-sun the hawker who said he saw two foreigners in uniform shining a torch into the creek, and who found and pulled the beggar from the creek, followed. He said that he usually went out to buy vegetables at 3 a.m., but on that night he did not go because he lost some time in saving the man from the creek.

Mr. Reeks I put to it you that you saw the car not in front of your house but in front of the Shanghai Power Company?--No, it was in front of my house.

I put it that the two foreigners you saw did not have a torch of any kind?--Why should I tell a lie?

Did you see the light of the torch?--Yes.

There is no electric street light for 60-80 yards on either side of your house?--I don't know.

Then how did you take the car number? The car had a tail light.

And you saw by the tail light the number of the moving car? --Yes. I was immediately behind the car as it was driven away.

The case will be resumed this morning at 10 a.m.

Reporting the proceedings of Saturday last concerning the argument by Mr. Reeks that the written statement of Doo Tsung-pu should be produced, our report said that "Mr. Reeks indicated that he would even be justified in stealing it."

Mr. Reeks informs us that the correct report should be: "Mr. Reeks intimated that if the document were not produced, he would give secondary evidence of it, that he would be entitled to do so even if he had stolen the document, and that apart from any question as to that act, the document would nevertheless be admissible."

《大美晚报》，1935年12月20日，星期五

垂死乞丐案中
陈述受到质疑

警察司机的书面陈述被采纳为证据；
辩护律师就“落水”的区别进行辩论

昨天上午，在对上海公共租界工部局警务处警佐 E. W. 彼得斯（E. W. Peters）和见习警佐 W. A. 朱德（W. A. Judd）提起的诉讼听证会上，律师进行了辩论，并对据称在11月30日凌晨从虹口港救出患病乞丐马德彪（Mau Tuh-piau，即马德标）的证人进行了交叉质询。这些人因袭击和非法杀人指控，在英国地方法官（C. H. 海恩斯先生，Mr. C. H. Haines）面前接受预审。

华捕3067号杜宗普（Doo Tsung-pu，音译）于12月2日向贝内特督察作出的一份书面陈述被作为证据提交，这份陈述引起了辩护方 H. A. 里克斯（H. A. Reeks）先生的激烈争论，因为他要求出示该文件。

证人再次出庭作证时说，他认为他之前作出的陈述（书面陈述）与他在法庭上的说法大致相同。他说他之前并未陈述他亲眼看到乞丐击中水面。他看到的是他被扔下去。他坚持认为他的书面陈述中并没有说他亲眼看到乞丐击中水面。

他还说他听到了落水声，但没有看到水花。

协助救人

斐伦路491号的店主郭世元（Kwok Sai-yuen，音译）说，事发当晚他正准备睡觉时，听到外面有人喊“救命”。他跑下楼，看到邻居孙金生（Sung Ching-sun）正在河边拉一个人上岸。他帮助孙某将那人弄上岸，随后一名中国警察赶来并叫了救护车。孙金生向警察作了报告，然后救护车赶到。

随后是对菜贩孙金生的交叉质询，他说他看到两名身穿制服的外国人用手电筒照向河里，并发现并将乞丐从河中拉出。他说他通常在凌晨3点出去买菜，但那晚他没有去，因为他在从河中救人上耽误了一些时间。

里克斯先生：我向你提出，你看到的车不在你家门前，而是在上海电力公司门前？——不，它在我家门前。

我提出，你看到的那两个外国人根本没有拿手电筒之类的东西？——我为什么要撒谎？

你看到手电筒的光了吗？——看到了。

你家两边60-80码范围内没有路灯？——我不知道。

那你是怎么记下汽车号码的？汽车有尾灯。

你是借着尾灯看清行驶中汽车的号码的吗？——是的。车开走时，我就紧跟在车后。

本案将于今天上午10点继续审理。

在报道上周六关于里克斯先生主张应出示杜宗普书面陈述的辩论过程时，我们的报道说：“里克斯先生表示，即使去偷取该文件也是正当的。”

里克斯先生告知我们，正确的报道应为：“里克斯先生暗示，如果不出示该文件，他将提供次要证据，即使他是偷来的文件，他也有权这样做，且除了关于该行为的问题外，该文件无论如何都是可采纳的。”

归档
MS
1235

COLLECTION OF AVIATION TAX FROM DANCING HALLS.

1935年12月17日。下午译件。

《时事新报》于12月15日发表如下评论：——

两名外籍巡捕将一名乞丐抛入河中。

本月一日，一名名叫马德标（馬德標）的南京籍男子，因病躺在新闸路（Sinkeepang Road）与北河南路（Point Road）路口。一名正在巡逻的中国巡捕发现了他，并将此事报告给卡德路（Kashing Road）巡捕房。两名外籍巡长彼得斯（Peters）和贾德（Judd）前往该地，将该男子带上他们的汽车。当车经过费伦路（Fearon Road）和鸭绿江路（Yalu Road）时，他们突然命令司机（一名中国巡捕）停车，随后将马德标抛入河中。这一行为被一名名叫孙金生（孫金生）的菜贩目睹，他从停泊在河中的一条船上借来一根竹竿，成功将马德标从河中救起。孙向虹口巡捕房的一名中国巡捕报告了此事，马被送往圣卢克医院（St. Luke's Hospital），但后来死亡。

自从这起残忍案件曝光以来，警方已在英国领事法庭对这两名有罪的外籍巡捕提起诉讼。目前尚不知判决结果如何。目睹如此极端的残忍行为，我们深感震惊；首先，这种行为是由“文明”的英国人犯下的，他们没有出于人道同情给予即时救助，反而将一名病人送上了死路；其次，即使是一名路过的摊贩也知道伸出援手是自己的责任，而这两名身为警务人员的英国人却未能履行这一职责，将该人送医治疗，反而以残忍的手段加速了他的死亡。

一方面，我们自然承认，这两名外籍巡捕的行为不能代表全体外籍巡捕或英国人的精神，但另一方面，我们认为应严厉惩处这些罪犯，以儆效尤；尽管警方已对罪犯提起公诉，但负责培训其成员的警务处不能推卸将警察职责托付给如此残忍和不人道者的责任。人们认为，警方最有必要严格调查其人员中是否仍存在其他残忍和不人道的成员，并就此发表官方声明，以安抚公众情绪并保障他们的安全。

12月14日下午2时，在中国航空公司会员征集团办事处（位于法租界蒙梯尼路（Rue de Montigny）青年会大楼）举行的会议上，李德超（Lee Deh Chao）主持并报告称，向各舞厅征收的航空捐（须贴附于各舞厅出具的账单上）将于数日后开始征收。

NICHI-NICHI

JAPANESE ARRESTED BY THE JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE.

On December 10 the Local
Japanese Consular Police arrested a Japanese named
K. Ohtsubo, age 36, at No. 63 Anloh Road, off Bubbling
Well Road for having run away from Dairen while he was
out from the gaol on Bail.

JAPANESE IMPRISONED FOR BEING DRUNK AND DISORDERLY

Yesterday morning, a Japanese
named K. Takemura, (fictitious name) age 35, was imprisoned
at the Japanese Consulate gaol for his disorderly
conduct at 2 a.m. December 10 in the vicinity of the
Chinese market on Jukong Road while he was under the
influence of liquor.

POLICE OFFICER'S REPORT OF O.K. AFTER THEY THREW
A BEGGAR INTO CREEK

The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi after
reporting the British Court's proceedings in connection
with the case involving a beggar victim and two police
officers, under the above heading, added a sarcastic
remark to the effect that instead of giving protection,
the police had thrown a Chinese pauper who was lying on
the street on a cold night, into a creek. "This shows
the nature of the protection given to the public by the
S.I.P. and explains what the Europeans think of the
Oriental people."

A KOREAN COMMITTED FOR TRIAL

Yesterday at the Japanese
Consular Court a Korean named Pak Dai Hyun, age 27, was
committed for trial on a charge of theft.

MAINICHI

S.M.P TO GIVE EXPLANATION TO THE JAPANESE AMALGAMATED
ASSOCIATION OF STREET UNIONS REGARDING THE ATTACK
ON MESSRS HIBINO YOKO.

At 4 p.m. to-day the Standing
Committee of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of
Street Unions will hold a meeting at the Japanese Club
when either Deputy Commissioner Tajima or Assistant
Commissioner Uyehara representing Major Bourne, Acting
Commissioner of the S.M.P. will attend the meeting to
give a sincere explanation in connection with the attack
on Messrs Hibino Yoko.

RICSHA COOLIE RUNS AWAY WITH A BAG CONTAINING VALUABLE
DOCUMENTS.

Yesterday afternoon a Japanese
reported to the Japanese Consular Police that a ricsha coolie
had run away with his leather bag containing a number of
bonds valued at Yen 87, which he had left on the ricsha.

C.A. Loh Sih Kya

Sir,
Acting on instructions of the D. C. (Special Branch)
the undersigned yesterday requested the management of the
"Sin Wan Pao" (新聞報), the "Shen Pao" (申報) and the
"Eastern Times" (時報) to refrain from commenting on the
case wherein two foreign policemen are being charged with
throwing a Chinese beggar into a creek until the British Court
had delivered its decision. The papers gave the undertaking
requested.

As the attitude of the "Central China Daily News"
(中華日報), official organ of Wang Ching Wei (汪精衛),
the "Shanghai Morning Post" (晨報), official organ of
General Chiang Kai Shek (介石), the "Min Pao" (民報),
official organ of the Kuomintang, and the "China Times"
(時事新報), official organ of Dr. H. H. Kung, towards the
Shanghai Municipal Police is not friendly, I did not approach
these papers but arranged with Chen Ko Zung (陳克成), Chief
of the Chinese Newspaper Censorship Bureau, to use his
influence to induce them not to comment on this case until

Clerical Assistant.

December 10, 1935.
Morning Translation
Chao Pao(早报), a mosquito newspaper, published the following comment on December 9 :-
THE UTTER DISREGARD OF HUMAN LIFE BY TWO FOREIGN POLICEMEN
Previously, a tragic case occurred at Fearon Road and Yalu Road corner when two foreign police "Lao Yah" ( Lords ) 老爺 were instructed to investigate into a case where a helpless Chinese was lying by the roadside. They, on this occasion, calmly finished the matter by throwing the Chinese into a creek without the slightest hesitation.
In this manner, the two foreign policemen had accomplished their duty, while at the same time, the worries of this poor Chinese who was unable to solve the problems of his own food and clothing were also settled. We cannot help admiring the knowledge and experience of these two foreign police "Lao Yah", and we hate those foreign police officers all the more violently for overlooking the life of this member of our weak race.
Such an act reflects the cruel thought of the imperialists in the sub-colonies. This fact cannot be camouflaged by the foreign gentlemen who always shout about humanity.
From the evidence of the statement made in the Court by the Chinese policeman who drove the two foreign policemen to Fearon Road, we are quite clear about the facts of this matter. The Police should therefore be held solely responsible. It is necessary for the British Consular Court in Shanghai to maintain the principles of humanity and to mete out strict punishment to the two foreign policemen.

蚊媒小报《早报》于12月9日发表如下评论：——

两名外籍巡捕对人类生命的极度漠视

此前，在费伦路和鸭绿江路转角发生了一起悲剧案件，当时两名外籍巡捕“老爷”（Lao Yah / Lords）奉命调查一起路边躺着一名无助中国人的案件。在此次事件中，他们毫不犹豫地冷静地将该中国人抛入河中，以此了事。
就这样，这两名外籍巡捕完成了他们的职责，同时，这名无法解决自身衣食问题的可怜中国人的烦恼也得到了解决。我们不禁钦佩这两名外籍巡捕“老爷”的知识和经验，同时也更加痛恨那些无视我们弱种族成员生命的外籍警官。
这种行为反映了帝国主义者在半殖民地中的残忍思想。这一事实是无法被那些总是高呼人道主义的外国绅士们所掩盖的。
从驾驶这两名外籍巡捕前往费伦路的中国巡捕在法庭上的陈述证据中，我们对这件事的事实已经非常清楚。因此，警方应承担全部责任。上海英国领事法庭有必要维护人道主义原则，并对这两名外籍巡捕予以严厉惩罚。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 11, 1935

Two Shanghai Policemen
Face Unlawful Killing
Count In British Court

Serious Charge Follows Death Of Alleged Victim,
A Beggar, From Pneumonia; Prosecution
Brings Record Of Calls At Station

SICK CHINESE "TOSSED INTO HONGKEW
CREEK LIKE A SACK OF COAL"

One of the most unusual cases in the history of the Shanghai Municipal Police came up in H. M. Police Court yesterday, for the first hearing of evidence against two members of the Force, Sergeant Ernest William Peters and Probationary Sergeant William Alfred Judd, on a charge of unlawfully killing a Chinese beggar by throwing him into Hongkew Creek. The prosecution yesterday, by means of police records and witnesses, traced the finding of a sick man in the early morning of December 1 and the report to Kashing Road Station. The Chinese driver of the two foreign policemen told of how the beggar had been picked up, groaning and unable to walk, and had been taken to Fearon Road and there tossed into Hongkew Creek "like a sack of coal that makes a big noise."

The man was eventually fished out by a Chinese hawker and others, according to evidence previously given at the inquest, but died last week from double pneumonia. A charge of assault was laid in H.M. Court last week, and yesterday Mr. John McNeill, prosecuting for the Crown and S.M.P., framed the additional following count:

"That you at 3 a.m. on December 1 in Fearon Road, threw Man Tuh-piau into Hongkew Creek thereby unlawfully killing him."

The charge of assault brought against the men before the death of their alleged victim also stands until the Magistrate (Mr. C. H. Harmer) has ruled on the case with reference to H.M. Supreme Court. Mr. H. A. Reeks, counsel for the defence, made an objection to continuation of the original charge which was noted.

Prosecution's Case

Two lines of evidence will be brought, Mr. McNeill indicated, the first coming from Kashing Road Police Station in the course of which certain events occurred —that a telephone message was received and the accused went out on search. The second concerns events at Hongkew Police Station at which a telephone message was received that a Chinese had been knocked down by a motor car and was taken off to hospital. It was not until December 3, Mr. McNeill emphasized, that the two cases were correlated—that the Chinese who who had been found by Hongkew Police was connected with events at Kashing Road. In the third place, medical evidence will be brought, he stated.

Finds Sick Beggar

Sung Chao-yin, C.P.C. 1728, attached to Kashing Road Station, said that while on his beat with C.P.C. 1903 about 2.40 a.m. on December 1, he saw a beggar lying on the pavement at the corner of Singkeipang and Point Roads. He telephoned to the station saying that the beggar was very sick. He was told to continue his beat, and when he turned about half an hour later the man was gone.

On December 3 he went to St. Luke's Hospital but could not see anyone who looked like the beggar.

(Makovetsky) to go on with the station car. Then Judd went out. Sergeant Peters told the witness to remain in the charge room. He saw Judd and Peters when they returned but absolutely nothing was said about the affair.

Driver Testifies

C.P.C. 3067, Doo Tsung-pu, said that he was on duty on the night of November 30—December 1 from 10 p.m. until 6 a.m., driving the station car, licence No. 8502. He was told to start up the car by the gateman, C.P.C. 3239, at about 2.45 a.m. He took with him F.S. 229 (Peters) and F.P.S. 106 (Judd). Peters told him to drive to Singkeipang Road. A dog was also with them.

The two men left the car and brought back out of an alleyway a beggar. They did not put him inside the car. Peters and the dog were inside the car, while Judd stood on the running board, where the beggar had been placed. They told the driver to "go ahead" and he drove from Singkeipang Road over the Hanbury Road Bridge to the corner of Nanzing Road. There was a telephone box there.

Peters said "Where are you going?" Witness replied: "Nowhere." He was then told to turn the car around and he did so, driving to Fearon Road past Yuhang Road Bridge, but not up to Yalu Road Bridge. He was told to stop the car. Both the men left the car. They removed the beggar and walked a few steps and threw the beggar away into the creek.

Saw Creek Affair

"I saw it with my own eyes," witness averred.

Afterwards the men returned to the car and witness drove to Kashing Road Station.

Cross-examination by Mr. Reeks followed.

Did you have no instructions except to drive ahead?—No. I turned into Hanbury Road because I thought they wanted to go to Hongkew because most of the beggars are usually taken there. I thought there was a place in Hongkew where beggars are usually kept.

I put it to you that the instructions you got were to drive to St. Luke's Hospital?—No. I was only told while driving to drive slowly.

I put it to you that the route you took was the route to St. Luke's Hospital?—Yes. But I had no instructions to go to St. Luke's.

Did you scan the beggar's features at the time he was first picked up?—No. It was raining at the time and I could not see his face clearly.

Answering a question by counsel, witness said that the beggar's body was mostly on the mudguard and partly on the running board.

I put it to you that when the men took the beggar from the car you did not get out of the car?—I did not get out of the car.

I put it to you that these men lifted the beggar, one taking one arm one taking another?—Peters got the right hand and right leg while Judd got the left hand and left leg of the beggar.

I put it to you that they then took him to the side of the creek and pushed him under the lower railing?—No. He was put over the top. At first I thought they were going to put the beggar on the pavement, but they walked a few steps and threw him over the rail.

Tossed Like Sack

Do you say that this man was tossed into the creek just as a sack of coal or something would be tossed into a place?—Yes. I think it was much like throwing a sack of coal. It makes a big noise when it hits the water.

I put it to you that you could not see the water from where you sat in the car?—I could not see

Cross-examined, the constable said that the man was very sick, foaming from the mouth and stiff in the legs. The witness then modified his story of the hospital visit to say that in a small room he had seen a man who had an appearance, or build, much like the beggar. His legs were stiff like the beggar's, but he could not positively identify him as the same man because the beggar had long hair, a muddy face and a beard about one quarter of an inch long. He was impressed by the similarity of the legs, which were uncovered on both occasions. The beggar was wearing short white pants which reached to the knees, he said.

Records Produced

Yuan Wong-hsing, clerk at Kashing Road Station, whose duty it is to answer the telephone, interpret and to record messages, said that on December 1 at 2.45 a.m. he had received a telephone message from C.P.C. 1728 regarding a beggar lying at the corner of Point and Singkeipang Roads. He identified the notation in the Street Message Book, Page 98, as follows:

December 1, 2.45 a.m.—from C.P.C. 1728. There is a beggar lying at Point Road near Singkei-Road being very serious. Clerk Yuan, F.P.S. 106, Judd attending.

Another notation which was not made in his presence, but which he identified as being in the handwriting of Sergeant Peters, said "on arrival the beggar had left."

Continuing, witness said that he had told Sergeant Peters about the message. Peters said "all-right." Judd, Peters, Sergeant Makovetsky, and Gateman 3239 were then in the charge room. Peters ordered the station car. Then Peters and Judd left the charge room, Sergeant Makovetsky remaining. In about 15 minutes they returned and witness asked what was the result of the case. Sergeant Peters replied "Everything is allright. O.K."

Sergeant Boris V. Makovetsky said he had seen Judd just before going on duty at 11 a.m. He saw him again in the charge room after 2.30 a.m. A telephone message had come through about a beggar at Point and Singkeipang Road, and Sergeant Peters had

《字林西报》，1935年12月11日，星期三

两名上海警察
在英国法庭面临
非法杀人指控

严重指控紧随一名据称受害者（乞丐）死于肺炎之后；检方出示警局出警记录

患病华人“像一袋煤一样被扔进虹口浜”

上海公共租界工部局警务处历史上最不寻常的案件之一昨日在英王陛下警察法庭开庭，首次对两名警员——巡长欧内斯特·威廉·彼得斯（Ernest William Peters）和试用巡长威廉·阿尔弗雷德·贾德（William Alfred Judd）——进行证据听证，指控他们通过将一名中国乞丐扔进虹口浜而非法将其杀害。昨日，检方通过警方记录和证人，追溯了12月1日凌晨发现一名病患并向嘉善路巡捕房报告的过程。这两名外籍警察的中国司机讲述了如何拾起那名呻吟且无法行走的乞丐，并将其带至斐伦路（Fearon Road），在那里将他“像一袋发出巨大声响的煤”一样扔进虹口浜。

根据此前在死因研讯中提供的证词，此人最终被一名中国小贩和其他人从水中捞出，但于上周因双侧肺炎死亡。上周在英王陛下法庭对该等人提出了袭击指控，昨日代表王室和工部局警务处起诉的约翰·麦克尼尔（John McNeill）先生提出了以下附加指控：

“你们于12月1日凌晨3点在斐伦路将万土标（Man Tuh-piau，音译）扔进虹口浜，从而非法将其杀害。”

在据称受害者死亡之前对该等人提出的袭击指控仍然有效，直至治安法官（C. H. Harmer 先生）参照英王陛下最高法院对此案作出裁决。被告辩护律师 H. A. Reeks 先生对继续原有指控提出异议，该异议已被记录在案。

检方案情

麦克尼尔先生表示，将提出两条证据线，第一条来自嘉善路巡捕房，期间发生了一些事件——收到电话留言，被告外出搜寻。第二条涉及虹口巡捕房发生的事件，当时收到电话留言称一名华人被汽车撞倒并被送往医院。麦克尼尔强调，直到12月3日，这两起案件才被关联起来——即虹口警方发现的华人与嘉善路发生的事件有关联。第三，他表示将提供医学证据。

发现患病乞丐

隶属嘉善路巡捕房的华捕1728号宋兆寅（Sung Chao-yin，音译）表示，12月1日凌晨2点40分左右，他与华捕1903号在辖区巡逻时，看见一名乞丐躺在新加坡路（Singkeipang Road，音译）和百老汇路（Point Road，音译）拐角处的人行道上。他打电话给巡捕房说这名乞丐病得很重。他被告知继续巡逻，当他约半小时后折返时，那人已经不见了。

12月3日他去了圣卢克医院（St. Luke's Hospital），但没看到任何看起来像那个乞丐的人。

（马科维茨基）继续驾驶警车。然后贾德出去了。彼得斯巡长让证人留在拘留室。他看到贾德和彼得斯回来，但关于此事只字未提。

司机作证

华捕3067号杜宗普（Doo Tsung-pu，音译）表示，他在11月30日晚至12月1日凌晨10点至6点值班，驾驶牌照号为8502的警车。凌晨2点45分左右，守门人华捕3239号让他发动汽车。他载上了外巡229号（彼得斯）和外试巡106号（贾德）。彼得斯让他开往新加坡路。还有一条狗跟他们在一起。

两人下车，从一条小巷里带出一个乞丐。他们没有把他放进车里。彼得斯和狗在车里，而贾德站在踏板上，乞丐就被放在那里。他们告诉司机“往前走”，他便从新加坡路开车经过汉伯里路（Hanbury Road）桥，开到南京路（Nanzing Road，音译）拐角处。那里有一个电话亭。

彼得斯问：“你要去哪里？”证人回答：“不去哪里。”随后他被告知掉头，他便照做了，驾车经过余杭路（Yuhang Road，音译）桥驶向斐伦路，但没有开到鸭绿江路（Yalu Road，音译）桥。他被告知停车。两人都下了车。他们搬下乞丐，走了几步，将乞丐扔进了浜里。

目睹浜边之事

“我亲眼所见，”证人断言。

随后这些人回到车上，证人开车返回嘉善路巡捕房。

随后由 Reeks 先生进行盘问。

除了向前开，你没有得到其他指示吗？——没有。我转入汉伯里路是因为我以为他们想去虹口，因为大多数乞丐通常都被带到那里。我以为虹口有个地方通常是安置乞丐的。

我向你指出，你得到的指示是开往圣卢克医院？——不。我只被要求在驾驶时慢点开。

我向你指出，你走的路线是去圣卢克医院的路线？——是的。但我没有接到去圣卢克医院的指示。

当第一次拾起乞丐时，你仔细看过他的面貌特征吗？——没有。当时在下雨，我看不清他的脸。

回答辩护律师的问题时，证人说乞丐的身体大部分在挡泥板上，部分在踏板上。

我向你指出，当那些人把乞丐从车上弄下来时，你没有下车？——我没有下车。

我向你指出，这些人抬起乞丐，一人抓一只胳膊？——彼得斯抓着乞丐的右手和右腿，贾德抓着左手和左腿。

我向你指出，然后他们把他带到浜边，把他推到下部栏杆下面？——不。他是被从上面扔过去的。起初我以为他们要把乞丐放在人行道上，但他们走了几步，把他从栏杆上扔了过去。

像扔袋子一样

你是说这个人就像扔一袋煤或什么东西进某个地方一样被扔进浜里的吗？——是的。我觉得很像扔一袋煤。掉进水里时发出很大的声音。

我向你指出，从你坐在车里的位置看不到水面？——我看不到

你第一次向上级官员提及此案是什么时候？我想是12月2日。我之前没提是因为涉事人员是我的上级。我之所以提起，是因为上级官员问起了此事。
**并未知情更多**
证人说他作了口头陈述，该陈述被记录下来并由他签字，他知晓文件内容。他否认在作陈述时，对此事的了解比事发几分钟后更多。他不知道后来有人从浜里被捞出来。
针对 Reeks 先生的问题：“你之前的陈述中是否有一部分是你亲眼看到乞丐落入水中”，麦克尼尔先生提出反对，治安法官予以支持。麦克尼尔先生辩称，既然原始陈述未作为证据提交，辩护律师不能试图通过提问来证明故事之间的差异。治安法官表示，如果 Reeks 先生愿意，他将允许就此点进行辩论。随后继续提问。
当第一次拾起乞丐时，他的衣服脏吗？——是的。他很肮脏，且在呻吟。
回答治安法官关于据称停车并将乞丐扔进浜里的斐伦路照明情况的问题时，证人说车后方有一盏路灯。

Doubt In Identity
Of Dead Beggar

Witness Not Sure Man
On Road Was One
In Hospital

Whether a beard a fraction of
an inch in length is a long beard
or not, and other matters of inter-
pretation, entered into a hearing
this morning in H. M. Police Court
when two Chinese connected with
the Kashing Road Police Station
gave testimony about incidents on
the early morning of December 1,
at Point and Sinkiepong Roads,
where a Chinese beggar who sub-
sequently died, is alleged to have
been thrown into a creek by two
foreign members of the Shanghai
Municipal Police, Sergeants E. W.
Peters and W. A. Judd.

Drawing attention to the differ-
ence in condition of the bedrag-
gled and muddy-faced beggar he
found lying on the pavement, and
the clean patient he saw in the
hospital later, Chinese Police Con-
stable No. 1728 declined to state
definitely that the two men were
the same.

"I saw that the beggar on the
road was very sick; he could not
move or talk and his legs were stiff,
so I telephoned the Kashing
Road Police Station....When I re-
turned to that place again more
than a half-hour later the man was
not there."

"By looking at the body of the
man in the hospital, he was very
much like the beggar, but the man
had no beard and his face and
head were shaved" the witness
said, after Mr. H. A. Reeks, attor-
ney for the defense, had objected
to the translator's first version,
which he claimed omitted the dis-
tinction between face and body.

Had Long Beard

Reexamining the witness, Mr.
John McNeill asked what kind of
hair the beggar had, and was told,
"A long beard, one-tenth of an
inch long. The face was dirty
and covered with mud, and his hair
was long."

Second witness was Yuan Wong-
hshih, English-speaking clerk at the
Kashing Road Police Station, who
reported having recorded a tele-
phone call on the date in question,
thus: "2:46 a.m. from C.P.C. 1723.
There is a beggar lying sick on
the Point Road, near Sinkiepong
Road, being very serious." Below
that entry was another made when
the witness was not there, but
which he identified as that of Ser-
geant Peters. It read, "On arrival
the beggar had left."

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1935年12月10日，星期二

死者乞丐身份存疑

证人不确定路上之人
即医院中之人

胡须长度仅几分之一英寸究竟算不算长胡须，以及其他解释性问题，成为今晨英皇陛下警察法庭听证会上的焦点。两名与嘉兴路巡捕房有关的华人就12月1日凌晨发生在百老汇路（Point Road）和新嘉坡路（Sinkiepong Roads）的事件作证。据称，一名随后死亡的华人乞丐被上海公共租界工部局警务处的两名外籍警士 E. W. Peters 和 W. A. Judd 扔进了一条小河沟。

华捕第1728号提请注意，他在人行道上发现的那名衣衫褴褛、满脸泥污的乞丐，与他后来在医院看到的洁净病人，状况截然不同，因此他拒绝明确断言这两人是同一人。

“我看到路上的病丐病情严重；他不能动也不能说话，双腿僵硬，所以我打电话给嘉兴路巡捕房……当我半个多小时后再次回到那里时，那人已经不在了。”

辩方律师 H. A. Reeks 先生反对译员的第一版翻译，声称其遗漏了面部与身体的区别。在此之后，证人说：“看了医院里那人的尸体，他和那个乞丐非常相像，但那人没有胡须，脸和头都刮过。”

留有长须

John McNeill 先生重新询问证人，该乞丐留着什么样的毛发，得到的回答是：“长胡须，十分之一英寸长。脸部肮脏且覆盖着泥土，头发很长。”

第二名证人是袁旺石（Yuan Wong-hshih，音译），嘉兴路巡捕房的英语书记员。他报告说在事发当日记录了一通电话，内容如下：“凌晨2:46，来自华捕第1723号。新嘉坡路附近百老汇路上有一名病丐躺卧，情况危急。”在该条目下方还有另一条记录，虽然当时证人不在场，但他确认为 Peters 警士所记。内容为：“到达时，乞丐已离开。”

December 9, 1935.
Morning Translation.

China Evening News (comment):

CHINESE THROWN INTO CREEK

On the morning of December 1, there appeared on Sinkeepang Road a Chinese male who could not speak. The man lay on the road motionless. It seemed that he was very sick. A Chinese policeman No. 1723 reported the matter to the Police Station by telephone, and two foreign policemen proceeded to the scene in a motor car. Unexpectedly, the two foreign policemen took the man into the motor car and threw him into a creek, resulting in his death.

Considering that the action on the part of the two foreign policemen is clearly contrary to the law, the Shanghai Municipal Police have filed a prosecution against them at the British Court.

From previous cases, we dare not imagine the consequence of the prosecution. We are really horrified at this remarkable kind of service rendered by the two foreign policemen! It seems that there will be a pardon granted to these two foreign policemen who look down upon the lives of the public, because they are to be pitied for their lack of knowledge. We are sorry for the Shanghai Municipal Police who are responsible for training and directing such foreign policemen. Unless such action on the part of the two foreign policemen concerned is regarded as being human kindness, the Shanghai Municipal Police must, at least, adopt certain appropriate measures to deal with such bad class policemen. On the contrary, will all the residents in the International Settlement still have such a lot of confidence on the Police Force?

In this semi-colony of Shanghai, the lives of the Chinese people are not considered by others, although we are faithfully crawling under the shelter of foreigners.

Central China Daily News (Comment)

At 2.45 a.m. December 1, a certain Chinese policeman saw a man lying unconscious on the ground at the corner of Sinkeepang and Point Roads. Later the Police Station despatched two foreign and one Chinese policemen to the scene to conduct enquiries. Unexpectedly the two foreign police officers threw the sick man into the creek. Fortunately the man was later rescued by a pedestrian, but he however died afterwards in the hospital.

On the morning of December 5 the two foreign police officers were sent to the British Court to be charged according to law. Legally speaking, the action on the part of these foreign officers constitutes a great violation of the law. Furthermore, their unlawful act was witnessed by the Chinese driver, G.P.C. 3067 and the pedestrian named Sung Ching Sung who rescued the deceased. 1935年12月9日。
晨间译文。

《中国晚报》（评论）：

华人被抛入河沟

12月1日上午，新嘉坡路上出现一名无法说话的华人男子。该男子躺在路上一动不动。看来他病得很重。华捕第1723号通过电话向巡捕房报告了此事，两名外籍警察驾车前往现场。出乎意料的是，这两名外籍警察将该男子带上汽车并把他扔进河沟，导致其死亡。

鉴于这两名外籍警察的行为明显违法，上海公共租界工部局警务处已向英国法院对他们提起诉讼。

从以往案例来看，我们不敢想象此次起诉的结果。对于这两名外籍警察提供的这种非凡“服务”，我们实在感到震惊！似乎这两名蔑视公众生命的外籍警察将获得赦免，因为他们因无知而值得怜悯。我们要为负责培训和指导此类外籍警察的上海公共租界工部局警务处感到遗憾。除非将这两名涉事外籍警察的行为视为仁慈之举，否则上海公共租界工部局警务处至少必须采取某些适当措施来处置此类劣等警察。反之，公共租界的所有居民是否还会对警力抱有如此多的信心？

在上海这个半殖民地，尽管我们忠实地匍匐在外人的庇护之下，但中国人的生命却不被他人所重视。

《华中日报》（评论）

12月1日凌晨2点45分，某华警看见一名男子昏迷不醒地躺在新嘉坡路与百老汇路交界处的地面上。随后巡捕房派遣两名外籍警察和一名华警前往现场进行调查。出乎意料的是，这两名外籍警官将这名病人扔进了河沟。幸运的是，该男子后来被一名路人救起，但随后在医院去世。

12月5日上午，这两名外籍警官被送往英国法院依法受审。从法律上讲，这些外籍警官的行为构成了严重违法。此外，他们的违法行为被华捕司机第3067号和救助死者的行人宋金生（Sung Ching Sung，音译）目击。因此，尽管华探从医院死者处获得的供词

page_data.en:
December 9, 1935. Morning Translation.

to the effect that he (the deceased) voluntarily jumped
the creek on that night might be beneficial to the foreign
policemen, it cannot be however relied upon, as the
deceased when saying this was likely in an unconscious
condition. Moreover even if the deceased did jump into
the creek voluntarily, the two foreign police officers
when noticing this should at least have rendered
assistance. Their failure in rescuing him therefore
constitutes a gross neglect of duty.
Although the deceased died of pneumonia,
it would not be at all impossible to save his life if
early treatment had been rendered. In view of all
these facts, it is quite clear that the action of these
two foreign officers was illegal and they should,
therefore, be punished accordingly.
page_data.zh:
1935年12月9日。晨间译文。

称他（死者）当晚是自愿跳入河沟，这可能对外籍警察有利，但这不可靠，因为死者说这话时可能处于无意识状态。此外，即使死者确实是自愿跳入河沟，这两名外籍警官在注意到这一点时至少也应提供援助。因此，他们未能施救构成了严重的失职。
虽然死者死于肺炎，但如果能及早治疗，挽救他的生命并非完全不可能。鉴于所有这些事实，这两名外籍警官的行为显然是非法的，因此应受到相应的惩罚。

December 8, 1935.
Morning Translation.
Sin Wen Pao and other local newspapers :-
TWO FOREIGN POLICEMEN THROW A CHINESE INTO A CREEK.
At 2.45 a.m. December 1, Chinese policeman No. 1728 attached to Kashing Road Police Station, while passing the corner of Sinkeepang Road and Point Road on patrol duty, saw a man sleeping by the side of the road. The man could not speak and it seemed that he was very sick. The policemen then reported the matter to the Police Station through telephone. Foreign Police Sergeant No. 229 E.W. Peters and Foreign Probationary Sergeant No.106 W.A. Judd took a Station motor car driven by Chinese policeman No. 3067 to the scene and brought the man into the car. When the motor car was passing the corner of Fearon and Yalu Roads, the two foreign policemen suddenly ordered the driver to stop the car and thereupon threw the man into the creek. The police officers then returned to the Police Station in the motor car.
Subsequently, a pedestrian named Sung Chin Sun(孙金生) gave assistance and dragged the man out of the creek. The matter was reported to Chinese policeman No. 993 attached to Hongkew Police Station and the man was removed to St. Luke's Hospital where he died at 8 a.m. December 6. The body was removed to the Fearon Road Mortuary.
Seeing that the two foreign Police officers had committed a crime, Hongkew Police Station escorted them to the British Court on the morning of December 5 and charged them according to law. The case was remanded until next Tuesday (December 10) and the two foreign Police officers were ordered to produce bails of £200 each. On December 6, Court doctors Wei Lih Kung(魏立功) and Chang Yen(张炎) of the First Special District Court visited the mortuary together with the doctors of the S.M.C. and held an inquest on the man.
At 10 a.m. December 7, Procurator Kou Wei (郭) of the First Special District Court, accompanied by the two Court doctors Wei and Chang and Clerk Wong Tsho Yih(王祖翼), after inspecting the body of the deceased, held the inquest.
Foreign Inspector Bennett stated the case. Witness Sung Chin Sun made the following statement :- "I am a native of Shanghai, age 26, residing at No. 493 Fearon Road and I am a vegetable hawker by profession. At 3 a.m. on that day, I went out and saw a motor car parked by the side of the creek. Two foreign policemen were leaning over the railings beside the creek and looking at the water. One of the policemen used a flash light. I noticed that the number of the motor car was 8502. Afterwards I saw the two policemen boarding the motor car which was driven away. I then ran to the side of the creek and saw the deceased. I borrowed a bamboo pole from a boat moored by the side of the creek and with the pole I saved the man out of the water. In the meantime, I was crying out 'Help, help.'"
Kuo San Yuen Tse(郭三元子) stated:- "I am a native of Kno Yeu(高郵), Kompo, aged 31, residing at 491 Fearon Road, and owner of a small shop. At 2 a.m. on December 1, I had already gone to bed. Upon hearing cries

1935年12月8日。
晨间译文。
《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：
两名外籍警察将一名华人抛入河沟。
12月1日凌晨2点45分，隶属嘉兴路巡捕房的华捕第1728号在巡逻经过新嘉坡路与百老汇路交界处时，看见一名男子睡在路边。该男子不能说话，看来病得很重。警察随即通过电话向巡捕房报告此事。外籍警士第229号 E.W. Peters 和外籍见习警士第106号 W.A. Judd 乘坐由华捕第3067号驾驶的巡捕房汽车前往现场，并将该男子带上车。当汽车经过斐伦路（Fearon Road）和鸭绿江路（Yalu Road）交界处时，这两名外籍警察突然命令司机停车，随即将该男子扔进河沟。随后警察乘车返回巡捕房。
此后，一名名叫孙金生（Sung Chin Sun）的路人施以援手，将该男子从河沟中拖出。此事报告给了隶属虹口巡捕房的华捕第993号，该男子被送往圣路加医院，于12月6日上午8时死亡。遗体被移至斐伦路殓尸所。
鉴于这两名外籍警察犯了罪，虹口巡捕房于12月5日上午将他们押送至英国法院并依法起诉。案件延期至下周二（12月10日）审理，两名外籍警察被责令各缴纳200英镑保释金。12月6日，第一特区法院的法医魏立功和张炎会同工部局医生前往殓尸所，对该男子进行了验尸。
12月7日上午10时，第一特区法院检察官郭伟（Kou Wei，音译）在两名法医魏、张及书记员王祖翼（Wong Tsho Yih，音译）的陪同下，在查验死者遗体后进行了验尸。
外籍督察 Bennett 陈述了案情。证人孙金生作了如下陈述：“我是上海人，26岁，住在斐伦路493号，职业是菜贩。当天凌晨3点，我出门看见一辆汽车停在河沟边。两名外籍警察正俯身在河沟旁的栏杆上看着水面。其中一名警察使用了手电筒。我注意到汽车号码是8502。随后我看见两名警察登上汽车驶离。于是我跑到河沟边，看见了死者。我从停靠在河沟边的一艘船上借了一根竹竿，用竹竿将那人从水中救出。在此期间，我一直在喊‘救命，救命’。”
郭三元子（Kuo San Yuen Tse，音译）陈述道：“我是高邮（Kno Yeu，音译）人，31岁，住在斐伦路491号，是一家小店的店主。12月1日凌晨2点，我已经上床睡觉。听到呼救声

December 8, 1935. Morning Translation.

for help, I got up and ran to the scene finding that Sung
Chin Sun had pulled out the deceased from the creek. I
helped Sung to drag the deceased out of the water and saw
the deceased spitting foam from his mouth."
Chinese policeman No. 3067 made the
following statement:- "At 2.45 a.m. that day, I drove the
motor car. I saw the two foreign policemen throwing the
deceased into the creek."
Chinese detective Shih Kwei Tsung(石貴春)
attached to Hongkew Police Station stated:- "I went to
St. Luke's Hospital to make an investigation. I questioned
the deceased who said that his name was Mr Teh Piao(馬德標),
a native of Nanking, aged 48, who had come from his native
place and could not find his friends and that he jumped
into the creek on that day as he could not get food. When
speaking, the deceased seemed having lost consciousness and
he talked slowly."
The Procurator delivered the following order:-
"The deceased named Mr Teh Piao, male, died due to pneumonia.
According to investigations made by the Police and to
statements made by witnesses, the deceased was pushed into
the creek by two British Police officers named Peters and
Judd. Since the two officers have been prosecuted by the
Police at the British Court, the case is to be dealt with
by the British Court. The body of the deceased is to be
encoffined by the Po Zai San Tsang Benevolent Institution."

后，我起身跑向现场，发现孙金生已将死者从河沟中拉出。我帮助孙金生将死者拖出水面，看见死者口中吐出泡沫。”
华捕第3067号作了如下陈述：“当天凌晨2点45分，我驾驶汽车。我看见两名外籍警察将死者扔进河沟。”
隶属虹口巡捕房的华探石贵春（Shih Kwei Tsung，音译）陈述道：“我去圣路加医院进行了调查。我讯问了死者，他说他叫马德标（Teh Piao，音译），南京人，48岁，从老家来此，找不到朋友，因为弄不到食物，所以当天跳入河沟。说话时，死者似乎神志不清，语速缓慢。”
检察官下达了如下命令：“死者名为马德标先生，男性，死于肺炎。根据警方调查及证人陈述，死者是被两名名为 Peters 和 Judd 的英籍警察推入河沟的。由于警方已在英国法院对这两名警官提起诉讼，本案将由英国法院处理。死者遗体由普善山庄收殓。”

December 7, 1935. Morning Translation.

Society Evening News and other local newspapers:

TWO FOREIGN POLICEMEN THROW A BEGGAR INTO A CREEK

At 3 a.m. on December 2, foreign Police officers Nos. 106 and 229, attached to Kashing Road Station, took the Station motor car which was being driven by C.P.C.3067, and went for a drive. When they were proceeding along Fearon Road by Hongkew Creek, at about 3.15 a.m., F.S. 106 saw a beggar sleeping by the side of the road, and immediately ordered the driver to stop the car. The two foreign Police officers then alighted from the car and ran over to the beggar who was sleeping at the side of the road, and catching him, one by the head and the other by the heels, heaved him into the Hongkew Creek, thus giving the beggar a cold bath. Luckily, a boatman belonging to one of the craft moored in the Creek, saw these two foreigners, Nos. 106 and 229, throw the beggar into the Creek. As the two foreigners drove off in the car, this boatman immediately dragged the beggar out of the Creek. Although the tide happened to be out at the time, the beggar lost consciousness owing to the extreme cold. The S.M.P. learning of the details of the case at 8 a.m. on December 2 removed the beggar to hospital at once, and suspended the two foreigners Nos. 106 and 229 from duty, keeping them under observation. On December 5, the beggar was still in hospital and the Commissioner of Police interviewed and questioned the two foreigners concerned. In view of the fact that this action on the part of foreign Police officers 106 and 229, was utterly uncalled for and contrary to any of the principles of human kindness, the S.M.P. intend to have these men very severely punished according to law.

Chen Pao (Shanghai Morning Post) and other local newspapers:

EXTRA-SETTLEMENT ROADS

It is learned that, as a result of negotiations held between Mr. O.K. Yue, Chief Secretary of the Shanghai City Government, and Mr. S. Fessenden, Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal Council, the Extra-Settlement roads question which has remained outstanding for some years may be settled in the near future. The authorities have not yet, however, made any definite statement. It is a fact that recently Mr. Yue and Mr. Fessenden have frequently met and discussed the subject.

According to information given out by the Shanghai Municipal Council, Mr. Fessenden will, in the near future, make public the documents containing particulars regarding the negotiations over the question.

1935年12月7日。晨间译稿。

《社会晚报》及其他本地报纸：

两名外籍巡捕将一名乞丐扔入河浜

12月2日凌晨3时，隶属于嘉兴路捕房的外籍巡捕第106号和第229号，乘坐由华籍汽车夫第3067号驾驶的捕房汽车外出兜风。凌晨3时15分左右，当他们沿斐伦路（Fearon Road）经过虹口河浜时，外籍巡捕第106号看见一名乞丐睡在路边，立即命令司机停车。随后，这两名外籍巡捕下车，跑向睡在路边的乞丐，一人抓住他的头，另一人抓住他的脚后跟，将他抛入虹口河浜，使该乞丐洗了一次冷水澡。幸运的是，停泊在河浜中的一艘船的船夫看见了这两名外籍人士（第106号和第229号）将乞丐扔进河浜。当这两名外籍人士驾车离去时，这名船夫立即将乞丐从河浜中拖出。虽然当时恰逢退潮，但乞丐因极度寒冷而失去知觉。上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）于12月2日上午8时获悉案情细节后，立即将乞丐送往医院，并暂停第106号和第229号两名外籍巡捕的职务，对其进行监视。12月5日，乞丐仍在医院接受治疗，警务处处长约谈并讯问了涉事的两名外籍巡捕。鉴于外籍巡捕第106号和第229号的这一行为完全毫无必要，且违背任何人道主义原则，上海公共租界工部局警务处打算依法对这些人予以严厉惩处。

《申报》（Shanghai Morning Post）及其他本地报纸：

越界筑路问题

据悉，由于上海市政府秘书长岳开先先生与上海公共租界工部局总办费信惇先生之间举行的谈判，悬而未决多年的越界筑路问题可能在不久的将来得到解决。然而，当局尚未发表任何明确声明。事实上，最近岳先生和费信惇先生已多次会面讨论此议题。

据上海公共租界工部局发布的信息，费信惇先生将在不久的将来公布包含有关该问题谈判详情的文件。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 8, 1935 1272J

Witness Testifies He
Saw Beggar Thrown In
Creek By 2 Foreigners

Pneumonia, Aggravated
By Water, Found
Death Cause

INQUEST HELD
OVER BODY

Conflicting Story Is
Credited Mendicant
On Deathbed

Death due to double-pneumonia, aggravated by water, was the coroner's verdict pronounced at the conclusion of the inquest held over Mau Tuh-piau, beggar, at the Fearon Road Mortuary yesterday morning. Mau is alleged to have been thrown into Hongkew Creek on the morning of December 1 by Sergeant Ernest William Peters and Probationary Sergeant William Alfred Judd, of the Kashing Road Police Station.

After rendering his verdict, the coroner stated that according to police investigation, the beggar had been thrown into Hongkew Creek by two British policemen, who had already been brought before H. M. Police Court on a charge of assault. He added that the body of the deceased would be handed over to the Tu-Soo Shing Ching Benevolent Society and be held pending the outcome of the case against the two police officers, scheduled to be resumed at 10.30 a.m. on the coming Tuesday.

Testimony Conflicts

Conflicting testimony featured the inquest yesterday in that a chauffeur of a police car declared that he saw the two policemen throw the beggar into the creek, while a Chinese detective from the Hongkew Police Station declared that he had questioned the beggar before the latter died on Friday morning, and had obtained information indicating that the man might have jumped into the creek himself.

Detective Inspector G. J. Bennett, of the Kashing Road Station, testified that at 2.45 a.m., December 1, he had received a telephone call from Chinese Constable 1728 that a sick beggar was lying on Singkeipang Road near Point Road. He continued that later, two foreign policemen, Nos. 399 and 106, had driven to the spot, had lifted the beggar to the running board of the police car they were driving in and that it was alleged that they had gone to Fearon Road. It was further alleged, the inspector continued, that they had thrown the beggar in the creek. Inspector Bennett did not publicly state the names of the two policemen but wrote the names down on a slip of paper, handing the paper to the coroner.

The man had been rescued from the creek, the witness continued by Tung Ching-sung, a hawker, who happened to be nearby. He continued that Chinese Police Constable 240, of the Hongkew Police Station, later took the beggar to St. Luke's Hospital, where the man died Friday morning.

Eye-Witness Testifies

Chinese Constable No. 1728 testified at the inquest, stating that he had found a sick beggar lying at the corner of Singkeipang Road near Point Road and had called the Kashing Road Police Station reporting the case. The driver of the police car, Police Chauffeur No. 3067, also testified. He declared that he was an eye-witness to the affair and actually saw the two policemen throw the beggar into the creek.

Tung Ching-sung, the hawker, who is stated to have rescued the beggar, declared that he did not actually see the beggar thrown into the water. He did see, he stated, two foreign policemen standing at the edge of the creek using a flashlight, evidently searching for something in the creek. They later got in their car and drove away. He continued that he went to the spot to investigate and suddenly heard feeble cries for help. He finally saw the beggar and getting a long bamboo pole, held it for the man to grab hold of. The beggar took advantage of his assistance, he said, grabbed the pole and the hawker pulled him to shore and up on the bank. Two other Chinese civilians who stated that they saw the rescue, told substantially the same story.

Beggar Questioned

At this juncture, Chinese Detective No. 240, of the Hongkew Police Station, testified that he had gone to the St. Luke's Hospital for the purpose of interrogating the beggar. That was on the following day, it was pointed out, and the beggar was too ill to speak. He called the next day, he said, and the beggar told him that he was 48 years old and a native of Nanking. The detective said he asked the man how he happened to be in the creek, adding that the beggar replied he was hungry and had no chow.

The detective then said that he asked the man if he jumped into the creek because he had no chow. He concluded his remarks by saying that the beggar answered yes. This brought an end to the proceedings, verdict was announced and the inquest closed.

《字林西报》，1935年12月8日，星期日 1272J

证人作证称
目睹两名外籍人士
将乞丐扔入河浜

肺炎，因浸水加重，
被认定为死因

举行尸体验尸听证会

相互矛盾的说法
据信来自临终乞丐

昨日早晨在斐伦路殓房举行的针对乞丐毛德标（Mau Tuh-piau）的验尸听证会结束时，法医裁定死因为双侧肺炎，因浸水而加重。据称，毛德标于12月1日上午被嘉兴路捕房的警长欧内斯特·威廉·彼得斯（Ernest William Peters）和见习警长威廉·阿尔弗雷德·贾德（William Alfred Judd）扔进虹口河浜。

法医在作出裁决后表示，根据警方调查，该乞丐是被两名英国巡捕扔进虹口河浜的，这两人已被带上英王陛下警察法庭，被控袭击罪。他补充说，死者的遗体将移交给杜肃生慈善会（Tu-Soo Shing Ching Benevolent Society，音译），并暂存以待针对这两名巡捕的案件结果，该案定于下周二上午10时30分继续审理。

证词相互矛盾

昨天的验尸听证会以相互矛盾的证词为特征，一名警车司机宣称他看到两名巡捕将乞丐扔进河浜，而一名来自虹口捕房的华籍侦探则宣称，他在乞丐于周五上午去世前曾对其进行讯问，并获得信息表明该男子可能是自己跳入河浜的。

嘉兴路捕房的探目 G. J. Bennett 作证说，12月1日凌晨2时45分，他接到华籍巡捕第1728号的电话，称有一名生病的乞丐躺在辛家牌路（Singkeipang Road）靠近百老汇路（Point Road，即今大名路）的地方。他接着说，后来，两名外籍巡捕（第399号和第106号）驾车到达现场，将乞丐抬到他们驾驶的警车的踏板上，据称他们随后去了斐伦路。这位探目继续说，据进一步指控，他们将乞丐扔进了河浜。Bennett 探目没有公开说出这两名巡捕的名字，而是将名字写在一张纸条上，递给了法医。

证人童景松（Tung Ching-sung，音译），一名小贩，继续作证说，该男子是从河浜中被救出的，他当时恰好在附近。他接着说，虹口捕房的华籍巡捕第240号后来将乞丐送往圣路加医院（St. Luke's Hospital），该男子于周五上午在那里去世。

目击者作证

华籍巡捕第1728号在验尸听证会上作证，称他在辛家牌路靠近百老汇路的拐角处发现一名生病的乞丐躺着，并致电嘉兴路捕房报告此案。警车司机、华籍汽车夫第3067号也作了证。他宣称自己是该事件的目击者，亲眼看到两名巡捕将乞丐扔进河浜。

据称救出乞丐的小贩童景松（Tung Ching-sung，音译）宣称，他并没有亲眼看到乞丐被扔进水里。他说，他确实看到两名外籍巡捕站在河浜边使用手电筒，显然是在河浜里寻找什么东西。他们后来上车驶离。他接着说，他前往现场查看，突然听到微弱的呼救声。他最终看到了乞丐，便拿来一根长竹竿，让乞丐抓住。他说，乞丐利用他的帮助，抓住了竹竿，小贩将他拉上岸并拖到堤岸上。另外两名声称看到救援过程的中国平民，讲述了大致相同的故事。

讯问乞丐

此时，虹口捕房的华籍侦探第240号作证说，他曾前往圣路加医院讯问该乞丐。有人指出，那是第二天，乞丐病重无法说话。他说他第二天又去了一次，乞丐告诉他，他48岁，南京人。这位侦探说，他问该男子是如何落入河浜的，并补充说，乞丐回答说他又饿又没有饭吃。

这位侦探接着说，他问该男子是否因为没有饭吃而跳进河浜。他最后说，乞丐回答说是。至此程序结束，宣布裁决，验尸听证会闭幕。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 7, 1935

VICTIM OF ALLEGED
ASSAULT DIES

Two Foreign Police Officers
Temporarily Suspended

INQUEST TO BE HELD
THIS MORNING

Mau Teh-piau, a Chinese beggar
whom two foreign members of the
Shanghai Municipal Police are accus-
ed of having thrown into the Hong-
kew Creek last Sunday, died yester-
day morning in St. Luke's Hospital.
He had been suffering from double
pneumonia and succumbed despite
strenuous efforts to save his life.
Sergeant E. W. Peters and Proba-
tionary Sergeant W. A. Judd, both
British, the policemen involved in
the case, have been suspended, pend-
ing further investigation.

At a hearing in H. M. Police Court
on Thursday, the Registrar, Mr.
C. H. Haines, sanctioned an applica-
tion of Mr. John McNeill, on produc-
tion of medical evidence, that a
deposition might be taken from Mau
Teh-piau. The deposition, however,
was not taken, as Mau remained in
a state of coma all Thursday.

The body of the deceased was re-
moved to the Public Mortuary yes-
terday morning, but it was then too
late for an inquest to be held. An
autopsy on the deceased's body was
made yesterday, however, by the
Court doctor, and an inquest will be
opened this morning.

The hearing of the case against the
two foreigners will be resumed in
H. M. Police Court on Tuesday at
10.30 a.m. Mr. John McNeill is con-
ducting the case for the prosecution
and Mr. H. A. Reeks is representing
the two defendants. Bail was al-
lowed both prisoners of £100 in
their own recognizance and two
sureties each of £100.

《字林西报》，1935年12月7日，星期六

涉嫌袭击案
受害者死亡

两名外籍巡捕
被暂时停职

今晨将举行
验尸听证会

中国乞丐毛德标（Mau Teh-piau），被指控于上周日被两名上海公共租界工部局警务处的外籍成员扔进虹口河浜，于昨日早晨在圣路加医院去世。他一直患有双侧肺炎，尽管 efforts 全力抢救，仍不幸身亡。涉案的两名英国巡捕，警长 E. W. Peters 和见习警长 W. A. Judd，已被停职，等待进一步调查。

在周四英王陛下警察法庭的一次聆讯中，书记官 C. H. Haines 先生批准了 John McNeill 先生的申请，在出示医疗证据后，允许对毛德标进行录供。然而，由于毛德标整个周四一直处于昏迷状态，录供并未进行。

死者遗体于昨日早晨被移至公共殓房，但当时已来不及举行验尸听证会。不过，法庭医生昨日对死者遗体进行了尸检，验尸听证会将于今晨开始。

针对这两名外籍人士的案件聆讯将于周二上午10时30分在英王陛下警察法庭恢复审理。John McNeill 先生代表控方出庭，H. A. Reeks 先生代表两名被告。两名囚犯均获准保释，每人自具保证书金额100英镑，并各有两名担保人，每名担保人担保金额100英镑。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

Two Foreign Police

INQUEST WILL BE
HELD THIS MORNING

Effort Made To Obtain

Mau Tuh-piau, beggar, alleged
to have been thrown into Hongkew
Creek on the night of December 1
by Sergeant Ernest William Peters
and Probationary Sergeant William
Alfred Judd, of the Kashing Road
Police Station, died at St. Luke's
Hospital late yesterday morning.
Although the inquest will not be
held until this morning, it is stated
by attending physicians that the
man was suffering from double
pneumonia. In the meantime, a
thorough investigation is being
conducted into the actual cause of
death in view of the importance of
the case.
Sergeant Peters and Judd were
charged in H. M. Police Court on
Thursday morning with assault,
causing actual bodily harm to the
beggar, and will be brought before
the court on Tuesday at 10.30 a.m.
for hearing.
British authorities declined to
comment on the matter yesterday,
even in view of the beggar's death,
merely, stating that the present
court schedule would be adhered to.
It was further reported that in
pursuance to an order issued by
H.M. Magistrate C. H. Haines at the
hearing on Thursday, an effort was
made to take a deposition from the
beggar. No comment was made,
however, on the success of these
efforts.
The assault is alleged to have
taken place on Faron Road during
the early morning hours of
December 1. No details connected
with the case have been revealed,
and in appearing for the Crown on
Thursday, Mr. John McNeill only
offered evidence of arrest.
The two sergeants were arrested
about 5 p.m. on December 1 at the
Kashing Road Police Station by
Detective Sub-Inspector John Mc-
Kenzie, in connection with the
case. The men were held in
the custody of Detective Sergeant
Bennett at the station and subse-
quently lodged in Ward Road Gaol
Court.
Mr. H. A. Reed is appearing on
behalf of the two accused, who
have been granted bail on two
sureties of $100 each, besides
$100 each in their own recogni-
zances.

案件中的中国人
在此死亡

两名外籍巡长
周二应诉

今晨将举行
验尸听证会

曾努力获取
死者供词

乞丐毛德标（Mau Tuh-piau），据称于12月1日晚被嘉兴路捕房的警长欧内斯特·威廉·彼得斯和见习警长威廉·阿尔弗雷德·贾德扔进虹口河浜，于昨日早晨晚些时候在圣路加医院去世。虽然验尸听证会直到今晨才举行，但主治医生表示，该男子患有双侧肺炎。与此同时，鉴于此案的重要性，正在对实际死因进行彻底调查。

彼得斯警长和贾德警长于周四上午在英王陛下警察法庭被控袭击罪，造成乞丐实际身体伤害，并将于周二上午10时30分出庭受审。

英国当局昨日拒绝就此事件发表评论，即使考虑到乞丐已死亡，仅表示将遵守目前的法庭日程安排。另有报道称，根据英王陛下裁判司 C. H. Haines 在周四聆讯中发布的命令，曾努力从该乞丐处获取供词。然而，对于这些努力是否成功，未作评论。

据称袭击发生于12月1日凌晨时分的斐伦路（Faron Road）。与该案相关的细节尚未披露，John McNeill 先生在周四代表王室出庭时，仅提供了逮捕证据。

这两名巡长于12月1日下午5时左右在嘉兴路捕房由副探目 John McKenzie 因本案被捕。这些人由探长 Bennett 在捕房拘留，随后被关押在华德路监狱法庭。

H. A. Reed 先生代表两名被告出庭，两人已获准保释，除每人自具保证书100美元外，还需两名担保人，每名担保人担保100美元。

CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 6, 1935.
（批：MUNICIPAL）
（批：S. B. REC）
（批：B. D. — 713）

Assault Charged To
2 S. M. Policemen

Foreigners Alleged To
Have Thrown Chinese
In Soochow Creek

EACH OFFICER PUTS
UP £100 AS BAIL

Plaintiff Reported
Near Death With
Pneumonia

One Chinese was reportedly near death yesterday as two British subjects, both members of the Shanghai Municipal Police, were brought to trial on charges of having assaulted him by throwing him into Hongkew Creek on December 1, thereby allegedly causing him bodily harm. The men who appeared in British Police Court at 9.30 o'clock yesterday morning are Sergeant Earnest William Peters and Probationary Sergeant William Alfred Judd.

The Chinese, one Mau Teh Piau, was reported at a late hour yesterday afternoon to be hovering near death in a local hospital and to be suffering from the effects of a serious case of pneumonia. His condition, it was alleged, was so weakened that he was lying in a state of coma and was unable to give evidence.

The charge against the two complainants as presented in court stated that the Chinese had been assaulted on December 1 last by the two members of the Shanghai Municipal Police by being thrown into Hongkew Creek. The men were arrested on Wednesday afternoon at the Kashing Road Police Station at approximately 5 o'clock, it was revealed. At the time of arrest both were cautioned and refrained from making any statement. Evidence of arrests was given yesterday by Detective John McFee of the Shanghai Municipal Police.

Following the rendering of evidence of arrest, Mr. John McNeill appearing on behalf of the complainant, asked for a remand and this was subsequently granted by Magistrate C. H. Haines and a re-hearing scheduled for Tuesday at 10.30 in the morning. Mr. H. A. Reeks, appearing for the two accused, asked that an order for bail be made by the court. Two sureties of £100 each were demanded. The accused were also prepared to place bail on their own recognizance to the amount of £100 each.

Mr. John McNeill, during the course of the hearing, suggested that evidence be taken from the complainant under Rule 9, and Mr. H. A. Reeks, speaking on behalf of the defendants stated that he was in accord with this request. It is understood that the man's condition will be carefully watched and if at any time he should be able to give a statement this will be taken without delay and might result in issuing a summons order against the accused. It is understood, however, that there is little hope of the plaintiff recovering enough to give evidence in the near future.

两名巡捕被控袭击罪

据称外籍人士将华人
抛入苏州河

每名警员缴纳
100英镑保释金

原告据报患肺炎
濒临死亡

昨日，两名英籍上海公共租界工部局警务处警员因被控于12月1日将一名华人抛入虹口港（Hongkew Creek），致其身体受伤，而被提堂受审。据报，该华人当时已濒临死亡。昨日上午九时三十分在英国警察法庭出庭的两名男子是警长欧内斯特·威廉·彼得斯（Earnest William Peters）和试用警长威廉·阿尔弗雷德·贾德（William Alfred Judd）。

这名华人名叫茅德标（Mau Teh Piau，音译），据报昨日下午晚些时候在当地一家医院中生命垂危，并患有严重肺炎。据称，他的身体状况极度虚弱，处于昏迷状态，无法提供证词。

法庭上提出的对两名被告的指控称，该华人于上月1日遭到两名上海公共租界工部局警务处警员的袭击，被抛入虹口港。据悉，这两人于周三下午五时许在嘉善路（Kashing Road）巡捕房被捕。被捕时，两人均受到告诫，并未发表任何声明。上海公共租界工部局警务处侦探约翰·麦克菲（John McFee）昨日提供了关于逮捕情况的证词。

在宣读逮捕证词后，代表原告的约翰·麦克尼尔（John McNeill）先生请求延期审理，此请求随后获裁判官 C. H. 海恩斯（C. H. Haines）批准，并定于周二上午十时三十分重新听审。代表两名被告的 H. A. 里克斯（H. A. Reeks）先生请求法庭下达保释令。法庭要求提供两名担保人，每人担保金额为100英镑。被告也准备以每人100英镑的金额具结保释。

约翰·麦克尼尔先生在听审过程中建议根据第9条规则录取原告的证词，代表被告发言的 H. A. 里克斯先生表示同意这一请求。据悉，院方将密切观察该男子的状况，若他任何时候能够陈述，将立即录取其口供，这可能会导致向被告发出传票。然而，据了解，原告在近期恢复健康至足以提供证词的希望渺茫。

A sick beggar found lying on the ground was 
removed by two foreign policemen in & motor car. Upon 
coming to a creek, the officers threw him into it. Such 
action is most improper. But the Foreign Settlements in 
Shanghai constitute a special world and Chinese people living 
in the Settlements receive special treatment. Foreign residents, 
especially Police officers in general and the foreign 
Police officers of the Foreign Settlements, regard Chinese 
in a special light, Thus, in the case of the beggar,

The two foreign policemen are being charged 
in the pritish Court and some 380 witnesses have been heard. 
On February 5, the chauffeur who drove the motor car 
conveying the beggar to the creek was questioned and on 
February 6 the hawker who rescued the beggar out of the water 
after he had been thrown into the creek was interrogated. 
It is said that more witnesses will be heard and that the 
case will be concluded next Tuesday or Wednesday. This 
shows how much attention the British authorities are 
paying to the case. The lawyers retained by the two 
foreign policemen are very fierce. On February 5, they 
questioned the chauffeur for over 6 hours and on the following 
day, the hawker was questioned. Thus the driver and the 
hawker may fall into traps laid by the lawyers. 

It has now been established that the sick beggar 
was not removed to a hospital but to the side of a creek; 
it has also been established that the beggar was thrown 
into the creek, The point as to whether the beggar fell 
on & beggar boat when he was thrown into the creek or 
whether the beggar was thrown into the creek itself has 
not yet been ascertained. If the beggar fell on the 
beggar boat, then the statement made by the hawker is false. 
For this reason the lawyers for the defence of the two 
foreign policemen on February 6 did their best to show that 
the hawker was a@ notorious character. 

We do not desire to comment on the case while 
it is sub judice. This case has drawn our attention to 
Police affairs in the Foreign Settlements and we take 
this opportunity to make the following observations:- 

Onecan notice on the streets at any time arbitrary 
acts committed by the lordly policemen who display their 
majesty to ricsha coolies, hawkers, prostitutes and beggars. 
Of course, in the eyes of the authorities of the Foreign 
Settlements, these people are so much filth, but however 
dirty they may be, they are human beings, althdugh :they 
are not treated as such. Licences of ricshas are teken 
away, their cushions are seized, the coolies kmeel on the 
road begging the policemen for their return. Stalls of 
hewkers are qaverturned with kicks and the wares scettered 
ebout on the ground :nd the hawkers nre token to the Police 
Station. In cold weather, prostitutes hurriedly run away 
at the approach of policemen. They :re detained in prison 
if arrested. &s to the trectment of beggnrs, the present 
case is 2 good example and needs no further comment. 

These men and women represent the lower section 
of the community. Whatever may be the condition of the 
Settlement, its foundations are based on this lower section 
of the community. Yet these people are being given such 
treatment! 

We may not hope that this small case will wake 
the authorities of the Foreign Settlements to their senses, 
but we do hope that it will serve 2s a clear warning to 
Chinese residents in the Settlements,
